title: Entero Healthcare Solutions Ltd - 544122 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Earnings Call Transcript

summary.headline: Entero FY26 revenue rose 31.5% like-for-like to INR6,591 crore with 4% EBITDA margin; FY27 guidance is 23% growth and 5% margin excluding new acquisitions.
summary.overview: FY26 met all three initial targets: like-for-like revenue growth of 31.5% (organic 15.6%, inorganic 16%), 4% EBITDA margin (+67 bps) and operating cash flow of INR96.2 crore. Q4 revenue grew 42.6% YoY, with organic growth of 17.1% and acquisitions contributing 26%, and Q4 EBITDA margin reached 4.5%. Minority interest jumped sharply in Q4 (about 38% of PAT) due to an abnormal, pulled-forward MedTech sale at a partly-owned subsidiary, which management says will normalise. FY27 guidance is 23% consolidated revenue growth excluding new acquisitions (about 11 points from calendarisation), 5% EBITDA margin, and at least 50% EBITDA-to-OCF conversion.

segments.name: MedTech
segments.commentary: Now above INR1,000 crore annualised revenue after 3 MedTech acquisitions in FY26 (Anand Chemiceutics, Ace Cardiopathy, Bio de Technology). Management says MedTech is over 15% of revenue, could reach about 20% in 2-3 years, and earns higher margins than pharma due to commercial/agency role.

segments.name: Pharma distribution
segments.commentary: Remains the core business with about 100,000 retail pharmacies, 3,600 hospitals, 97,500 SKUs and 3,300+ manufacturers. Management expects pharma and MedTech to contribute equally to FY27 organic growth.

segments.name: GLP-1
segments.commentary: Management says current GLP-1 sales are about INR10-12 crore per month, roughly 5% of industry GLP value, with a share above its overall India share due to cold-chain warehouses; included in FY27 guidance.

guidance_outlook: FY27 consolidated revenue growth of 23% YoY excluding new acquisitions; about 11 points from calendarisation of FY26 acquisitions and the rest organic (management also cited about 22% in one answer).
FY27 EBITDA margin of 5%, about 50 bps above Q4 FY26's 4.5%, from MedTech mix, operating leverage and exiting low-margin businesses.
EBITDA-to-operating cash flow conversion of at least 50% in FY27.
Tax rate of about 22-23% for FY27.
Minority interest to be about 25-27% of PAT before minority interest in FY27, down from about 38% in Q4.
Finance cost to stay relatively stable for a couple of quarters, then decline over the next couple of years as IPO funds were used up.
No new acquisitions assumed for the next 6-8 months; guidance would be revised upwards if acquisitions are made. Acquisitions are priced at 5-7x EV/EBITDA.
capex_capacity: Seven acquisitions closed in FY26, including 3 in MedTech; management says no new acquisitions are planned for the next 6-8 months, focusing on organic growth.
Some MedTech IVD machines are placed at customer sites on 5-year reagent rental contracts and are depreciated; cardiology and other MedTech lines carry little depreciating equipment.
Cold-chain facilities in all warehouses support GLP-1 distribution.
Depreciation rose about 50% QoQ in Q4, and interest costs rose because acquisitions were debt- or investment-funded after IPO proceeds were used up.
demand_pricing: Organic growth outperformed IPM by 1.6x for FY26 (15.6% vs IPM); Q3 and Q4 multiplier fell to about 1.4x as IPM grew about 12% versus 7-8% earlier, while organic growth stayed at 16-17%.
FY27 like-for-like growth is about 15% (1.5x IPM) per management; some low-ROIC businesses are being exited and some are now booked on a net-revenue basis, lowering reported revenue.
Gross margin gains come from scale purchasing and a commercial/agency role; full commercial role accounts for 10-15%+ of sales, with margins at least double normal distribution margins.
Management pointed to the 8-15% gross margin band on slide 28 for distribution; Q4 gross margin was 10.9%.
Middle East conflict: direct imports are a very small share of sales, so management says the company is largely insulated.

qa_highlights.question: Why did minority interest jump in Q4 and how much will it be in FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Q4 minority interest was abnormally high, about 38% of PAT, due to a customer pulling forward equipment sales at a partly-owned subsidiary. FY27 minority share is guided at about 25-27% of pre-minority PAT.

qa_highlights.question: Does the 23% FY27 growth include calendarisation and GLP-1?
qa_highlights.answer: Yes. Calendarisation is about 11 points, and GLP-1 is built into guidance, with the company taking a disproportionate share given its cold-chain network.

qa_highlights.question: Why is working capital falling, and how much working capital will FY27 growth need?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed the drop mainly to higher payables from MedTech, which has longer credit terms than pharma. Q4 annualised revenue of about INR7,600-8,000 crore means most working capital is already in the balance sheet, so incremental needs should be small.

qa_highlights.question: Will acquisitions continue, and at what valuations?
qa_highlights.answer: No new acquisitions are assumed for 6-8 months. Valuations remain 5-7x EV/EBITDA, and call options on remaining stakes are pre-agreed, typically over 3 to 5 years.

qa_highlights.question: What is the ROCE outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects FY27 ROCE above 20%, with further upside possible over time, though not necessarily in the near term.

qa_highlights.question: What is the company's competitive moat?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited a two-way network: about 100,000 customers and over 3,000 manufacturers. It said retail consolidation will stay limited, with chains under 15,000 stores versus over 1 million pharmacies.

risks_watch: Minority interest of 25-27% of PAT in FY27 materially reduces attributable earnings; watch for further put-option liability effects on net worth, which was flat in FY26.
Finance cost is expected to stay stable for a couple of quarters before declining; interest and depreciation rose sharply in Q4.
IPM growth outperformance has narrowed to about 1.4x as IPM rose to about 12%; FY27 organic growth depends on sustaining this.
FY28 growth not guided; management will provide more visibility in H2 FY27.
Payables-driven working capital improvement may reverse if MedTech mix or credit terms change; the 50% EBITDA-to-OCF target depends on this.
summary.management_tone: Confident on delivering FY26 targets and on FY27 margin expansion, but guarded on FY28 and interest costs. Management deflected several questions on minority interest and acquisition pipeline and offered to share some data offline.

So it's a 2-way moat. It's a 2-way closed-loop system.

financial_highlights.value: Not stated as a total; organic like-for-like growth 17.1%, acquisition-led growth 26%

growth.why: Management guides FY27 consolidated revenue growth of 23% excluding new acquisitions (about 11 points from calendarisation of FY26 deals, the rest organic, with FY27 like-for-like around 15%) and 5% EBITDA margin, backed by organic growth of 16-17% and MedTech mix, but no new capacity or order book figures were given.
